answer: A ripple-based reputation mechanism resists sybil attacks by propagating trust outward from a verified core through weighted interaction graphs. Each identity starts at an isolated knoll on the network edge, earning tiny trust increments from random established peers; confidence ripples inward only after repeated exchanges with differently located nodes. Since clones cluster to farm each other, they stay trapped in an outer spiral of mutual endorsements the algorithm discounts, so attackers pay full costs per duplicate while fake clusters' internal signals yield zero economic weight.
